detailed_rationale:
CAMS is India's dominant mutual fund Registrar & Transfer Agent, servicing roughly 68% of industry AUM (Rs 55.1 lakh crore as of Q4 FY26, up 21% YoY), with an essentially asset-light, high-return, near-monopoly business model (ROE 38%, ROCE 50%, D/E 0.05x, interest coverage ~98x). Q4 FY26 delivered the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 395.22 crore with PAT of Rs 125.44 crore and a 46.5% EBITDA margin. The quant data shows a meaningful gap between the 3-year revenue CAGR (~16%) and 1-year revenue growth (~6.6%): CAMS' own revenue growth is running well below the ~21% AUM growth the industry is enjoying, because RTA fees are charged as a shrinking basis-point yield on AUM (regulatory TER caps and price resets across the industry compress realized yield as AUM scales), so pure AUM growth does not translate one-for-one into CAMS revenue growth.

The multi-year growth story beyond core MF-RTA servicing is genuine diversification: CAMS is scaling non-MF, non-AUM-linked lines including KRA (KYC registration), insurance repository, NPS-CRA-adjacent services, CAMSPay, and account aggregator services, several of which management has flagged as approaching profitability and growing AUM-independent revenue faster than the core book (per company commentary, CAMS Finserv/non-MF AUM was cited growing ~22% with an eye on segment profitability). This diversification reduces single-client/regulatory concentration risk versus a pure MF-RTA model. At ~39x trailing earnings the stock is not cheap for a quasi-utility-like fee business, but the moat (68% market share, high switching costs, regulatory barriers to new RTA entry) justifies a premium versus a generic financial-services name; the real judgment call is how much future growth that premium already assumes.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold on both windows; nothing in fresh research changes that. This is a high-quality, near-monopoly, capital-light compounder (quality score in the high-90s) but revenue growth (single digits YoY) is decelerating relative to industry AUM growth due to yield compression, and the ~39x multiple already prices in a re-acceleration led by non-MF diversification that is still early-stage. Genuine business quality with a fair-to-slightly-rich valuation is consistent with Hold, not a Sell call.
summary: CAMS is the dominant record-keeper for India's mutual fund industry, a high-margin, capital-light business benefiting from the country's long-term shift of savings into mutual funds. Revenue growth has been slower than the industry's AUM growth because fees, charged as a small percentage of assets, get squeezed as the industry scales and regulations cap costs. The company is diversifying into new fee businesses (KYC records, insurance record-keeping, payments) to add a fresh growth leg. We rate it a Hold: an excellent business, priced for steady rather than spectacular growth.
positive_para: Structural, multi-decade tailwind from financialization of Indian household savings into mutual funds (record SIP registrations, up 19% YoY, and a unique investor base past 4.1 crore, up 27% YoY) underpins durable AUM growth for the industry CAMS serves. Near-70% market share with high client switching costs and regulatory barriers to new entrants gives pricing power and earnings visibility that few Indian financial-services businesses can match, evidenced by ROE of 38% and ROCE of 50% on a near-zero-debt balance sheet. Diversification into KRA, insurance repository, CAMSPay and account aggregator services gives a second growth leg that is not directly tied to the fee-compression dynamics of the core MF-RTA book.
negative_para: Core revenue growth (~6.6% over the last year per the quant data) is running well below industry AUM growth (~21% YoY) because RTA yields compress as AUM scales and regulatory TER caps push fee resets across the industry — this is a structural headwind to the core business, not a one-off, and it caps how much of AUM growth CAMS can actually capture as revenue. At ~39x earnings, the market is already crediting the newer, smaller diversification businesses with meaningfully closing that growth gap; if KRA/insurance-repository/CAMSPay scale-up disappoints or takes longer than expected, the stock has limited room for multiple expansion from here.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~39x trailing earnings for a business now growing revenue in the high single digits, the multiple is fair-to-full for what the core MF-RTA franchise alone can deliver; it is only comfortably justified if the non-MF diversification (KRA, insurance repository, CAMSPay, account aggregator) scales fast enough to lift blended growth back toward the low-to-mid teens over the next few years. The near-monopoly moat and 38% ROE argue for paying a premium versus a generic mid-cap financial, but this is a quality-at-a-fair-price situation, not an obviously cheap one.
